Pusalotas Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Pusalotas was served in the early 20th century by Rav Yakov Kalmus (1904–1910), who went on to become Chief Rabbi of Moscow (1926–1935) before moving to Israel, where he sat on the Chief Rabbinate and served as a judge on the High Rabbinical Court. The town's Jewish community was also home to Reuven and Frida Brog, whose grandson Ehud Barak later served as Israel's Chief of General Staff and Prime Minister. In August 1941, 248 of Pusalotas's Jews were shot in the Sadeikoniai forest, and ten more were shot directly at this cemetery that July. This is considered one of the best-preserved Jewish cemeteries in Lithuania, with nothing built on its grounds during the Soviet era; it was digitized in 2007 by Howard Margol and Yulik and Daniel Gurevich.
